worksheet.title: Sort Two Ways
worksheet.subtitle: The same things, grouped two ways
worksheet.learning_goal: I can sort the same shapes by more than one rule.

parts.title: One pile, two ways to sort
parts.text: The same shapes can be grouped in more than one way. It depends on the RULE you choose. Here is Bit's pile.

parts.title: Way 1 — sort by shape
parts.prompt: Rule: same shape together. Draw the circles in one box, triangles in the next, the star in the last.

parts.title: Way 2 — round or pointy?
parts.prompt: New rule: round shapes (●) in one box, pointy shapes (▲ ★) in the other. Sort the SAME pile again.

parts.title: You try — sort this pile two ways
parts.prompt: Pile: ★ ● ▲ ●. First sort by shape. Then sort by round or pointy.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: The same things can be sorted in different ways — you just change the rule. Computers sort by different rules too: by size, by colour, by name.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children sort one pile two different ways — by exact shape, then by round-versus-pointy. Seeing the same set grouped different ways is a first thinking-skill behind coding — the rule decides the groups. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child draws into the group boxes. Optional: a small pile of shape blocks to sort by hand two ways.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Name the pile — two circles, two triangles, one star.
2. Do one together. Way 1: sort by shape (Ex 1). Way 2: change the rule to round versus pointy (Ex 2) — circles are round; triangles and the star are pointy.
3. Let them try. Children sort the Exercise 3 pile both ways on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Way 1 (by shape): circle = 2, triangle = 2, star = 1. Way 2 (round vs pointy): round = 2 (the circles); pointy = 3 (two triangles + one star).
Exercise 3 pile (star, circle, triangle, circle) — by shape: star 1, circle 2, triangle 1. Round/pointy: round 2, pointy 2.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: re-sorting Way 2 by shape out of habit. Restate the new rule (round vs pointy).
Make it easier: do only Way 1 with hands-on blocks, then add the second rule.
Make it harder: invent a third rule together (big vs small, or has-a-point vs no-point).
Make it active: sort the children themselves two ways (e.g. by sleeve colour, then by shoe type).

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children classify the same objects by more than one attribute.
In plain terms: the same pile can be grouped different ways depending on the rule.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child sorts the one pile correctly under both rules and can say that changing the rule changes the groups.
